{{Quote|For every sin there is an equal and positive retribution.|Saying from the Holy-Book of the Sacred Way|<ref name="marvel7" />}}
The '''Sacred Way''' was a religion that was active in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] during the era of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Among the Sacred Way's core beliefs, outlined in its [[Holy-Book]], were the value of the [[Soul/Legends|soul]] of organic beings and the idea that every [[Sin/Legends|sin]] was met with retribution. Followers of the Way settled the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]] and set up an agrarian society there&mdash;when offworlders began to flock to the world, the Way was represented in the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] of [[Tun Aduban]] by the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]] [[Priest/Legends|priest]] known only as "[[Pera]]." Notable Followers of the Way included [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Peccati Syn]], who was raised in the religion before it was outlawed on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].

==Practices and beliefs==
{{Quote|Half human&hellip; half mechanical droid. Yet the man half of him had a soul&hellip; or so my faith believes.|"Pera"|<ref name="marvel7" />}}
[[File:Sacredwayburial.jpg|thumb|250px|"[[Pera]]" performs a [[Sacred Way/Legends|Sacred Way]] burial ritual, with [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] as spectators.]]
The Sacred Way drew its teachings from its [[Holy-Book]], a text that contained teachings on [[Sin/Legends|sin]], the nature of the [[Soul/Legends|soul]] and other musings. The Sacred Way had [[Priest/Legends|priests]], who oversaw church operations from missions on [[Planet/Legends|planets]] with a Sacred Way presence.<ref name="marvel7" /> These missionaries were tasked with finding converts in their communities, but were noted by locals as not being overzealous in pushing their faith.<ref name="gamer">{{GamerCite|4|The Starhoppers of Aduba-3}}</ref> Those priests wore [[Color/Legends|lavender]] [[Robe/Legends|robes]] and oversaw the burial of the [[Death/Legends|dead]]. This extended to deceased [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborgs]], which often proved highly controversial on worlds with a large anti-cyborg sentiment. Sacred Way burial rites involved an eerie, chirp-like chanting to the [[Space-gods|gods of space]], along with the burning of [[Incense/Legends|incense]].<ref name="marvel7" />

Although cyborgs were only partially organic, Sacred Way priests believed that the organic part had a soul and thus deserved a proper burial. According to Sacred Way belief, the belongings that a person had upon them at the [[Time/Legends|time]] of their death belonged to the one that buried them. Although Sacred Way priests were capable of defending themselves, they generally detested violence, believing that it only led to more violence. This tied in with the religion's concept of sin, as it was written in its Holy-Book that every sin was met with equal retribution.<ref name="marvel7" /> The Sacred Way also had the concept of an afterlife, which promised glories to the religion's believers.<ref name="insider">{{InsiderCite|66|Who's Who: Imperial Grand Admirals}}</ref> Adherents to the Sacred Way were referred to as Followers of the Way.<ref name="gamer" />

==History==
{{Quote|Begone, defilers of the Sacred Way!|"Pera"|<ref name="marvel7" />}}
[[Standard century/Legends|Centuries]] after the [[New Sith Wars]], a group of Followers of the Way, searching for a quiet retreat, settled the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]]. The Followers set up small agrarian communities governed in accordance with their religious tenets, surviving almost entirely on [[maze-stalk]]. When a [[Chromium/Legends|chromium]] rush resulted in Aduba-3 being flooded with offworlders, the Sacred Way responded by setting up a mission in the newer [[Spaceport/Legends|Spaceport]] of [[Tun Aduban]]. By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the outpost was headed by a<ref name="marvel7" /> [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]]<ref name="gamer" /> priest referred to as "[[Pera]]."<ref name="marvel7" /> Although religion was more or less abolished on some worlds after the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]&mdash;leading one young former Sacred Way follower, [[Peccati Syn]], to join the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] and eventually become a [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]]&mdash;Pera continued to practice in Tun Aduban throughout the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="insider" />

Among other duties, Pera oversaw the burial of former [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] on [[Spacer's Hill]] outside of town, according to local tradition.<ref name="marvel7" /> Although he was generally well respected by the locals,<ref name="gamer" /> Pera's sometimes ran Pera into trouble with [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]], who detested cyborgs and refused to allow them to be laid to rest with their fellow pilots.<ref name="marvel7" /> Although one dispute in 0 ABY turned violent, passing [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] backed Pera up and helped him perform the burial rite.<ref name="marvel7" /> In the years to come, legend spread that the religion's [[Sacred Way founder|founder]] had established a monument on [[Hoogon Two]], which became a destination for a group of Sacred Way pilgrims. The travelers managed to book passage to Hoogon Two with spacers [[Khedryn Faal]] and [[Marr Idi-Shael]], only to discover to their crushing disappointment that the monument did not exist.<ref name="crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Sacred Way was introduced in [[Star Wars (1977) 7|''Star Wars'' (1977) 7]], written by [[Roy Thomas]] and [[Howard Chaykin]] and released in [[1977]].<ref name="marvel7" /> Over twenty years later, additional information on the religion was given in ''[[The Starhoppers of Aduba-3]]'', which appeared in the magazine [[Star Wars Gamer 4|''Star Wars Gamer'' 4]].<ref name="gamer" />
